title: QUIC RFC 9000 S9P6P1 Preferred Address Conveyance And Per-Family Selection Verification
verification_method: Focused S9P6P1 requirement-home tests over preferred_address TLS conveyance and per-family selection, followed by the TLS transport-parameter canary, Release build, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, full Release test suite, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers the remaining generated non-clean S9P6P1 preferred-address conveyance and per-family selection tail.
expected_result: The focused tests show that server preferred_address is carried in the TLS EncryptedExtensions transport-parameters extension, both IPv4 and IPv6 families survive server encoding and client parsing, and the client selects the preferred address family matching the original server path family.
procedure: Run the focused S9P6P1 remaining-tail requirement-home filter.
Run the tight TLS transport-parameter canary.
Run the full Release test suite without rebuilding.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The S9P6P1 preferred-address handshake-confirmed transition remains closed under ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0080.
The S9P6P1 preferred-address validation-failure policy remains closed under ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0081.
The base runtime path-validation model remains owned by ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0001.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim public preferred-address configuration APIs, public migration APIs, multipath support, hosted interop readiness, or closure of deferred fuzz obligations.

status_summary: Local verification on 2026-05-06 passed: focused S9P6P1 remaining-tail requirement-home filter 3/3; tight TLS transport-parameter canary 5/5; Release build 0 warnings/errors; regenerated QUIC coverage triage 1,316/1,771 trace-clean; SpecTrace core validation 490 artifacts; full Release no-build suite 4,580/4,580. git diff --check is recorded in the final closure report.
